documents.search:
A manageable learning path

Guide home

   First pass: understand the player experience

Read Controls, then chapters 02–12. Start the title, create/use a spare save slot, explore with each character, talk to NPCs, and use Items/Equipment/Shop. For each feature, answer:   What triggers it? What changes? What feedback shows the change?  

   Second pass: understand world generation

Read 13–18 and 26. Draw a 5×5 water pool with two rings. Trace one WFC collapse/propagation step. Draw a simple room tree, identify its parent chain and branch degree, then explain where keys and locks go. Distinguish the room graph from floor WFC.

   Third pass: understand battle

Read 19–24. Trace encounter hit → BattleSession → layout setup → player turn → enemy turn → result → return. Use the skill table for each character and demonstrate SP/AP/cooldown gates. Explain shield consumption and projectile interception before discussing fancy effects.

   Fourth pass: understand minigames

Read 25–28. Work through one simple molecule naming example, then one Berdly attack/defend turn. For rhythm, calculate one note's score and one half-completed hold. Explain which minigame unlocks which ultimate and why dungeon entry depends on both.

   Fifth pass: prepare the explanation criteria

Read 00, 01, 03, 04, 07, 13, 19, 26, and 29. These cover Git, OOP, settings persistence, binary saves, raycasts, WFC, FSM, naming, and feedback. Use the demonstration checklist and the workbook row pages for completeness.

   For each chapter

1. Read only its plain explanation first.
2. Find the named class/method in the linked script.
3. Trace the call into its next owner (data, character state, UI, or session).
4. Demonstrate its normal behavior and one blocked/edge case.
5. Say the short answer aloud in your own words.

Do not memorize an entire 1,000-line controller. Read the exact branch for the selected character/skill, then inspect the shared helper it calls.

documents.search:
Controls by context

Guide home

Keys do different things in different modes. Exploration reads the Player map; battle has a separate Battle map; chemistry and rhythm consume their own UI/minigame inputs.

   Exploration / dungeon

  Input   Action  
  ---   ---  
  WASD   Move the active character.  
  Space   Jump; hold for Druid slow-fall; swimming uses its own vertical response.  
  1 / 2 / 3   Select WiSe / RandaL / Druid.  
  F   NPC/chest/door interaction; WiSe cutting; RandaL placement toggle. Context gates apply.  
  Left mouse   Confirm RandaL's valid book placement.  
  Q / E   Change the configured exploration camera view.  
  Scroll   Zoom camera; map focus can direct scrolling to map zoom.  
  M   Toggle minimap.  
  Esc   Gameplay menu / close the active relevant overlay.  
  Ctrl   Open/close the cheat console.  

   3D battle

The following binding table was read directly from the saved Battle input-action asset.

  Action   Binding  
  ---   ---  
  Move (Up)    <Keyboard /w   
  Move (Down)    <Keyboard /s   
  Move (Left)    <Keyboard /a   
  Move (Right)    <Keyboard /d   
  ChangeCharacter    <Keyboard /c   
  EndTurn    <Keyboard /t   
  Skill1    <Keyboard /1   
  Skill2    <Keyboard /2   
  Skill3    <Keyboard /3   
  Skill4    <Keyboard /4   
  FastForward    <Keyboard /5   
  Confirm    <Mouse /rightButton   
  Charge    <Mouse /leftButton   
  Dodge    <Keyboard /space   

Select skill 1–4, then right-click to confirm. A/D while aiming rotates WiSe's crescent or cycles RandaL's target. During Arcane Barrage, hold/release left mouse to charge/fire. During WiSe dodge, Space dodges and right-click counters after a perfect input. In Jevil's panel, WASD moves the heart.

   Berdly chemistry

Choose Attack/Defend through the buttons, then click an answer or press 1–4. These numbers answer the molecule question, rather than changing the overworld character. The timer continues through guessing/console behavior described in the minigame chapter.

   Pink rhythm / Grand Ensemble

W/A/S/D match chart lanes. Press for taps and keep held for holds. Extra unmatched presses are ignored by the scoring rules. Follow the countdown/audio timing rather than the character movement map.

   Input ownership

Dialogue, shops, challenges, entry modals, menus, travel, and the cheat console use blocking flags. A key used inside an overlay should not also trigger an exploration action. Inspect NPCChallengePrompt.BlocksGameplayInput when debugging input conflicts.

   Input assets

- InputSystem_Actions.inputactions — included asset.
- Battle.inputactions — included asset.

documents.search:
Reading the workbook and its scores

Guide home

The source is !Scoring Game 26-2 JT.xlsx. It has 21 sheets: Result, Master, 17 scored categories, and two supporting rubrics ( Rythm Game  and  IUPAC Algorithm ). The workbook was read without modification.

   How a normal rubric row calculates

A section allocates points from its category maximum. Row weight divides that allocation between requirements. Most rows then use  harvested = score / 4 × row maximum . Scores are assessment inputs from 0–4. Master sums category harvested points.

The stored Result!B6 value is   36.043791666666664 out of 100  . It is a cached workbook result, not a new score for the current game. The copy was not recalculated. Zero scores must not be treated as proof a feature is missing.

  Category   Maximum   Stored harvested   Checklist  
  ---   ---   ---   ---  
  General   3   0.18   General  
  Main Menu   1   0   Main Menu  
  Settings   2   0   Settings  
  Save File   2   0   Save File  
  Characters   5   3.72917   Characters  
  NPC   3   2.25   NPC  
  Item   2   2   Item  
  Equipment   2   2   Equipment  
  Shop   2   1.94667   Shop  
  Overworld   13   3.12813   Overworld  
  Dungeon   20   18.4333   Dungeon  
  Battle   7   2.3765   Battle  
  Boss Battle   6   0   Boss Battle  
  Skills   12   0   Skills  
  Enemies   5.5   0   Enemies  
  Minigame   12.5   0   Minigame  
  Cheats   2   0   Cheats  

   Special scoring dependencies and inconsistencies

-  Minigame!F18  multiplies its IUPAC row by the supporting  IUPAC Algorithm!F3  result and that row's score.
-  Minigame!F39  multiplies its rhythm row by  Rythm Game!F3  and the row's score.
-  Skills!F111  multiplies the healer rhythm allocation by  Rythm Game!F14  and its score.
-  IUPAC Algorithm!F9  scales the algorithm subtotal by  C11 , whose factor comes from the two separate question scores.
-  Dungeon!E8  records score   1  ,  C8  records maximum   6  , but  F8  is manually stored as   5  . The ordinary score/4 rule would give 1.5. Preserve the workbook's actual 5 while explaining the mismatch.
- Some Master Realized cells are manual values, including Save File, Dungeon, Battle, and Boss Battle. They are not all formulas even when a nearby category uses E/C.

The scoring guide preserves recorded numbers and flags these distinctions. It does not repair the workbook or infer an official grade. Exact requirement labels, source rows, recorded inputs, and code/teaching links are in the per-sheet checklist files.

   Study priority

The largest category maximums are Dungeon (20), Overworld (13), Minigame (12.5), and Skills (12). Study their algorithms and demonstrations carefully, but also prepare the explanation criteria: OOP, binary rationale, raycast, FSM, and shared naming.

   Source versus request

The workbook's requirement text is source material used to organize the guide. It is not authorization to edit features or assessment cells. Your direct request was to read and explain the game in Markdown with linked scripts. Project AGENTS.md requirements were retained and mismatches were reported.

documents.search:
Demonstration and practice checklist

Guide home

Use a spare playthrough. These are suggested demonstrations, not a report that this task ran them.

   Menu, settings, and save

-     Title, Play, Settings, Exit, and Continue behave correctly.
-     Title shows all required character models and distinct animations; Play animation is visible.
-     Music and SFX levels work independently across scene travel.
-     FPS/resolution/window settings apply and restore.
-     Three slots are independent; show saved level/playtime/location.
-     Save & Quit succeeds before leaving; reload party/items/settings/world seed.
-     Explain header/version/checksum and why binary is used.

   Exploration

-     Move/jump/switch all three; white highlight, switch effect, and HUD remain correct.
-     Only WiSe's player interaction cuts trees/cactus and breaks dungeon props.
-     RandaL previews and rejects blocked/steep/out-of-range book placement.
-     Druid slows falling while Space is held and clears it after switching.
-     Fixed seed reproduces layout; fresh games normally use new seeds.
-     Actual WFC-selected prefabs are Unity Terrain for grass/water/sand/rock.
-     Water pool is 5×5; complete sand then grass/rock rings survive diagonal/chunk checks.
-     Required pool boat and deck chest are present.   Known failure: current path creates a cliff.  
-     Opened chest persists after chunk reload and save restoration.
-     Walking sounds are distinct for all four terrain types.   Known failure: water maps to rock.  
-     Streaming loads nearby chunks and removes distant object/data allocations.
-     Trees/cactus drop resources; rock/mushroom pickup increments Resources.
-     NPCs/landmarks/healing/decorations/enemies use valid placement.
-     Rain/blossom behavior is located and demonstrated; source review did not locate it.
-     Maps, camera view changes, zoom, and menu respond in context.

   Inventory, NPCs, and shops

-     F completes typed dialogue, then advances/opens interaction.
-     Yes/No prompt blocks world input and selects the correct minigame.
-     Items show previews, remove one copy, and hide zero quantity.
-     Diamond revives; normal potions reject dead/full-ineligible targets.
-     Gear equips/removes in two slots with correct stat differences and no refill exploit.
-     Shop quantity/price/gold/error flow works; Diamond is excluded.
-     Merchant removes only its assigned resource type.

   Dungeon

-     Entry requires both relevant ultimate unlocks.
-     Explain random walk, weighted edges, Kruskal, parent/branch chain assignment.
-     Show Spawn, Guide, Boss, Normal, Treasure, and Enemy content.
-     Keys are available in intended chains and locks consume original keys once.
-     Explain room graph generation separately from floor WFC.
-     F gate/chest/door/break interactions show their real feedback.
-     Map reveals neighbors, tracks visits, draws connections/portrait, rotates/pans.
-     Different entrances retain separate layouts/progress; Continue resumes first room.

   Battle and skills

-     Actual melee/projectile hit starts combat with a fade and random saved layout.
-     Movement range, basic lock, two AP, SP/cooldown/unlock checks work.
-     Normal/veteran enemy turns and cover interception are visible.
-     Damage formula, shield absorption, healing popup, death, and Diamond revival are explainable.
-     Use all twelve ability paths and show correct indicators/effects.
-     Show WiSe kill reset, three-shield cap, five-round-robin fireballs, dodge timing/counters.
-     Show RandaL lock switching, SP buff, portal cooldown scope, charged first-person barrage.
-     Show Druid burst/pull/teleport validation and rhythm-driven charm.
-     Show Jevil dialogue, summons/kidnap, all five patterns, and invincibility.
-     Win grants party EXP; return location/defeated encounter persist.
-     Menu items/save behavior and fast-forward respect each sequence's timing.

   Minigames and explanation

-     Name a simple molecule: longest chain, numbering, branches, multipliers, tables.
-     Explain that dungeon degree is chain nesting, not node neighbor count.
-     Berdly correct/incorrect/timer flow, Attack/Defend, two protected hits, and unlock.
-     Pink tap/hold timing, score weights, stamina, and 84,000 unlock threshold.
-     Parse one actual beatmap tap and one hold from milliseconds to seconds.
-     Demonstrate cheat input ownership and wrong-area rejection.
-     Explain OOP, ScriptableObjects, event channels, Input System, and Git/GitHub using project examples.
-     Measure optimization with Profiler evidence and inspect responsive UI at supported sizes.

Record the observed result and current seed/scene beside any failure. Historical PASS files do not replace a fresh run.

documents.title: Small glossary
documents.search:
Small glossary

Guide home

  Term   Meaning in this project  
  ---   ---  
  MonoBehaviour   Unity component attached to a GameObject; receives lifecycle callbacks.  
  ScriptableObject   Configurable asset data, such as an Item or BattleSkill.  
  Prefab   Saved object hierarchy instantiated by code.  
  Awake / Start   Initialization callbacks; GameSave's early order matters for restoring the seed.  
  OnEnable / OnDisable   Register/unregister actions/listeners as components activate.  
  Update / LateUpdate   Frame updates; late updates can follow earlier movement.  
  Coroutine   A sequence that can yield over frames, used for typing, fading, and attacks.  
  Event channel   An asset exposing events so publishers and HUD listeners share a connection.  
  Singleton   One accessible owner instance, used for systems such as PlayerInventory.  
  Seed   Initial random-generator input; combined with stable coordinates/salts for reproduction.  
  Salt   Extra seed input separating random streams for different content.  
  Chunk   A finite square section of streamed overworld tiles.  
  Domain   Possible tile choices still allowed for one WFC cell.  
  Entropy   A measure of uncertainty; lowest unresolved weighted entropy selects the next world cell.  
  Collapse / propagation   Choose one WFC option, then remove incompatible neighbor options.  
  TerrainData   Height/paint data used by a Unity Terrain instance.  
  Raycast   Collision query along a ray; used to find book-placement ground and blockers.  
  Overlap box / sphere   Collision query for objects within a volume.  
  NavMesh / agent   Walkable navigation data / component following paths on it.  
  FSM   Named states with conditions/actions; used by encounter enemies.  
  AP / SP   Turn action points / character skill resource.  
  Cooldown   Remaining unavailable-turn count for a skill, retained by the character.  
  Pooling   Reusing visual objects rather than recreating them repeatedly.  
  Tree graph   A connected graph without cycles; used for molecules/dungeon topology.  
  Kruskal / disjoint set   Sorted-edge tree construction / structure detecting already-connected nodes.  
  Locant   One-based branch position used for naming.  
  Dungeon degree   Recursive chain nesting depth, distinct from graph node degree.  
  DSP clock   Audio timing clock used by the rhythm controller.  
  Judgement   Timing/completion category that determines rhythm reward.  
  Binary schema   Agreed field types/order/version for saved bytes.  
  Checksum   Corruption detection hash; not encryption.  
  Additive scene   A scene loaded alongside the existing scene to retain party/world state.  
  PlayerPrefs   Stored application preferences; not the full playthrough save format.

documents.search:
Git, GitHub, and explaining optimization

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    General .

   Git and GitHub

Git records version history locally: working files → staged changes → commit. A branch is a movable label for a line of commits. GitHub hosts repositories for sharing, remote backup, and review. A commit can exist locally without being pushed to GitHub.

The inspected repository contains commits about enemy patrols/attacks, boss projectile speed, travel transitions, arrival feedback, Berdly animation, and dungeon generation limits. This shows local history. This documentation review did not inspect GitHub push timing, so “push periodically” needs remote evidence if assessed.

   Explain a useful commit

Describe the concrete behavior changed and why. Keep one coherent change per commit when practical. Read  git status  before staging so unrelated changes are not included. The working tree already had edits in BattleCamera.cs and BattleController.cs when this guide was created; their current contents are captured in the script copies.

   Optimization mechanisms in your game

  Mechanism   What work it reduces   Tradeoff to explain  
  ---   ---   ---  
  Nearby chunk streaming   Number of live world Terrain/content objects.   Generation/unload can still cause spikes.  
  Map redraw on tile/room change   Repeated texture rebuilding.   Camera/UI transforms still update.  
  Batched dungeon floor meshes   Separate material draw submissions.   Mesh building costs time and memory.  
  Pooled rhythm/boss visuals   Repeated Instantiate/Destroy churn.   The pool keeps spare objects in memory.  
  RaycastNonAlloc/OverlapBoxNonAlloc   Per-query result-array allocation.   Full buffers must be handled correctly.  
  Independent seeded data   Reproduction and stable content queries.   Determinism does not by itself make code faster.  

“Optimized” should be demonstrated with Unity Profiler measurements of frame time, allocations, memory, and generation cost under a representative playthrough. No such new measurement was made for this task. Avoid claiming a frame rate from the target-FPS setting alone.

   How to read before editing

Start with a feature's owning controller and follow its calls. A MonoBehaviour lives on an object, a ScriptableObject lives as data, and an Editor script is tooling. Check scene/prefab references before deciding a missing callback means missing behavior.

   Scripts to read

- WFCWorldManager.cs — included copy.
- DungeonGenerator.cs — included copy.
- BattleBossGame.cs — included copy.
- PinkRhythmController.cs — included copy.

   Demonstrate it yourself

Show the local commit history and explain one coherent change. In Unity Profiler, compare steady walking with crossing a chunk boundary and name the CPU/memory work being measured. This guide does not contain a fabricated benchmark.

   Explain it in one answer

“Git tracks changes locally; GitHub shares the repository remotely. Streaming, batching, and pooling reduce specific work, but optimization must be supported by runtime measurements.”

   Exact workbook requirements covered here

The row number is the source locator. The rubric file preserves recorded scores separately.

-  General!B19 : Push into github periodically — rubric row.
-  General!B20 : Using github's commit best practices — rubric row.
-  General!B21 : Understand the difference between git and github — rubric row.
-  General!B22 : Understand why use git — rubric row.

documents.search:
OOP, ScriptableObjects, and event channels

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    General .

   What this feature does

The game divides responsibilities between reusable data, live character state, controllers, and UI. Start with this chapter before reading the larger controllers.

   The four OOP pillars in your code

  Concept   Plain explanation   Your example  
  ---   ---   ---  
  Encapsulation   Keep state behind methods that apply its rules.    CharacterBase  keeps current HP/SP private.  Heal ,  SpendSP , and  Equip  update them and notify the HUD. Some public fields still expose configuration directly, so encapsulation is selective.  
  Inheritance   A specific type reuses the common behavior of a parent.    WiSe ,  RandaL , and  Druid  inherit  CharacterBase . NPC variants inherit  NPCBase .  
  Abstraction   Expose a useful interface without requiring callers to know every implementation detail.    Item  and  NPCBase  are abstract base classes. A shop can work with an  Item  reference.  
  Polymorphism   The same operation can behave differently for different types.    Equipment.Cost  and  Consumable.Cost  override  Item.Cost ; NPC subclasses override approach/dialogue behavior.  Consumable.Use(CharacterBase)  is an overload, not an override of  Use() .  

   How ScriptableObjects work here

 CharacterData  stores starting stats.  Item ,  Equipment ,  BattleSkill ,  DungeonSettings , and audio settings store editable asset data. A  .cs  file defines the shape; a  .asset  file contains a configured instance. Runtime HP, EXP, and ultimate unlocks belong to the character instance, so unlocking a skill does not rewrite the shared starting asset.

   How the HUD event channel works

1. A stat method changes the character.
2.  NotifyStatsChanged  raises  CharacterStatsChanged  on the assigned channel.
3. HUD scripts subscribed to that asset update their display.
4. Selection uses the separate  CharacterSelected  event.

The publisher does not need to know which HUD is listening. Both sides must use the same event-channel asset. Subscribe in  OnEnable  and unsubscribe in  OnDisable  to avoid stale listeners.  IntEventChannel  is another available channel type; its existence alone does not prove a particular scene uses it.

Music, SFX, frame rate, resolution, and fullscreen

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Settings .

   What the player changes

Music and SFX have separate levels. FPS choices, resolution, and window mode affect the application across scenes.

   How it works

 SettingsUI  reads saved preferences in  Awake . Left/right resolution buttons choose among 1280×720, 1920×1080, and 3840×2160.  ApplySettings  calls  Screen.SetResolution  and saves width, height, and fullscreen preference. The fullscreen toggle changes the mode immediately and stores it.

 FPS  exposes the frame-rate button handlers.  GameAudio  routes music and effects into separate mixer groups, stores volume preferences, and applies them centrally.  GameAudioBootstrap  makes settings available when scenes start.  GameAudioMenuUI  connects the in-game sliders to the same audio behavior.

   Why it survives a scene change

 PlayerPrefs  keeps application settings. Scene audio sources are routed to shared mixer groups, so adjusting the group affects multiple sources. Save slots additionally capture  SaveGameSettings , allowing a loaded playthrough to restore its saved configuration.

   Things to explain precisely

- A target FPS is a limit/request, not a guarantee the hardware can sustain that rate.
- Selecting a resolution and applying it are separate operations.
- The fullscreen button text describes the alternative action ( Windowed  while fullscreen is active).
- Muting SFX should not mute music. Test both independently.

For the “configuration affected every scene” criterion, demonstrate a setting before and after travel rather than pointing only at PlayerPrefs calls.

documents.search:
Three binary save slots and restoring a playthrough

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Save File .

   What gets saved

Three independent  slot-1.sav  through  slot-3.sav  files live beneath  Application.persistentDataPath/Saves . They contain party stats/progress, equipment, inventory copies, gold, selected character, world seed/settings, position, opened chests, defeated encounters, audio/display settings, playtime, and visited dungeon layouts/progress.

   Saving, step by step

1.  GameSave.Capture  converts live scene state into plain  SaveData .
2. Items/equipment are recorded by names resolved through the item catalog.
3.  BinarySaveFile.Write  validates the data and writes primitives/arrays in a fixed order.
4. A header stores  WISE , schema version 3, payload length, and SHA-256 checksum.
5. The complete temporary file replaces the prior file. Save & Quit returns to the title only after a successful write.

   Loading, step by step

Read verifies size, version, checksum, and value bounds before scene restoration. GameSave runs early and installs the saved world seed before generation. Later it restores party/inventory and dungeon progress, then reveals the scene.

Version 2 binary saves are readable. A legacy version 1 JSON file has a one-time import path. A checksum detects corruption; it is not encryption or proof a file has not been deliberately edited.

   Why binary is used

Fixed primitive values avoid JSON field-name/text-number overhead and make the schema explicit. The tradeoff is that reader and writer must agree on field order and version. This uses BinaryReader/BinaryWriter, not BinaryFormatter.

   Restore behavior to remember

- Continue is based on   last played  , not only last saved.
- A dungeon save resumes in its first room with its layout/progress, not the exact saved room position.
- An ordinary battle save restores the encounter return position; it does not resume halfway through an attack animation.
- Save is rejected during travel.
- Deletion requires the title UI confirmation and affects one slot.

Seeds reproduce generated terrain under the current algorithm. Changing that algorithm can require save migration even if the stored seed stays the same.

Movement, switching characters, HP/SP, EXP, and HUD

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Characters ,  Overworld ,  Dungeon .

   What the player does

WASD moves; Space jumps; 1/2/3 chooses WiSe/RandaL/Druid during exploration. The active character's HUD shows its live state. Battle uses a separate character-selection system.

   Movement flow

The generated Input System wrapper supplies movement/jump actions.  CharacterMovement  turns input into camera-relative horizontal motion, applies gravity/jump logic, and moves a CharacterController. Jump buffering and fresh ground contact help the jump respond near landings. Swimming is selected from WFC water plus actual water-bed depth and controller height.

Breaking a decoration temporarily blocks movement/switching and advances a timed animation/impact sequence. Gameplay overlays also block input, so pressing movement or number keys inside a modal does not control the exploration character.

   Switching flow

 SwitchToCharacter  remembers the previous position/rotation, activates the requested character there, disables the others, and broadcasts selection events. The camera and WFC streamer receive the new transform. A configured particle prefab is spawned on subsequent switches. White highlighting belongs to renderer/outline setup plus  ObjectHighlight .

   Stats and progression

 CharacterBase  owns current HP/SP, level, EXP, ultimate unlock, two equipment slots, and four battle cooldowns. EXP uses   100 per level   with remainder carried forward. Level gain changes level/EXP here; these methods do not automatically increase the base attack/HP data just because the level rose.

Maximum stats and attack/defense/crit equal starting CharacterData values plus equipped bonuses. Equipping clamps current HP/SP down to a reduced maximum; it does not refill them when a larger maximum is equipped. Stat and selection events refresh the HUD.

  Important distinction:   disabling an exploration character during switching does not delete its stats. All party members still exist and can be saved or healed.

WiSe: cutting trees and cactus, and breaking decorations

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Characters ,  Overworld ,  Dungeon .

   What this ability does

WiSe is the exploration character for destructive interactions. Trees/cactus produce resource pickups; dungeon breakables use a timed swing/impact and may drop coins.

   How tree cutting works

 WiSe.Update  reads F directly through Input System's  Keyboard.current  and searches for a suitable nearby  TreeCuttable . It coordinates the character's breaking animation with the cut.  TreeCuttable.Cut  checks a  cut  guard, creates its configured loot, disables colliders, requests navigation rebuilding, and destroys the object.

Each loot entry specifies an Item and amount.  WorldRandom.AtPosition  derives a repeatable drop random stream from world seed, X/Z position, and a salt. Drops become sprite objects with trigger pickups and bobbing visuals. Inventory receives one item per collected copy.

   How dungeon breaking differs

 DungeonGenerator  manages the interactable decoration and its room progress.  CharacterMovement  sequences windup, sound, and impact. A destroyed decoration can be recorded in the dungeon snapshot, so it stays broken after restoration.

   Why only WiSe should cut

The gate belongs to the interaction/controller path, not the low-level  TreeCuttable.Cut  method: another programmer could call that method directly. Demonstrate the actual player flow with another selected character to prove the restriction.

   Persistence limit

SaveData explicitly persists opened chests, defeated enemies, and dungeon breakables. It does not contain an overworld cut-tree or collected-resource list. A regenerated chunk can recreate those resources. Do not claim resource depletion survives every chunk unload or Continue.

Read the Inspector loot table to explain   what   drops; the code explains   how   those entries become pickups.

RandaL: book preview, raycasts, and placement constraints

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Characters .

   What the player sees

With RandaL selected, F toggles placement mode. The ghost book turns green on a valid location and red on an invalid location. Left-click commits a valid placement; F cancels.

   What a raycast means here

A raycast asks which collider a line from an origin in a direction intersects.  Camera.ScreenPointToRay  turns the cursor into a world ray.  RaycastNonAlloc  stores its hits in a reusable array. The code picks the nearest acceptable hit instead of assuming the returned array is sorted.

   Placement checks, in order

1. A usable camera and mouse exist and the cursor is inside the camera view.
2. A solid hit exists; a filled hit buffer is rejected conservatively.
3. The hit is within the maximum distance from RandaL.
4. Its layer and slope are allowed. In the active overworld it must be a TerrainCollider.
5. The preview's visible bounds produce an overlap box.
6. Other solid objects must not overlap that box; a filled overlap buffer is rejected.

The preview ignores its own colliders. Visual bounds align the bottom of the book with the hit surface. The placement camera, ground layers, distance, and slope limits are Inspector configuration.

   Committing a placement

 TryPlaceBook  runs the checks again on the click so a stale green preview cannot bypass a newly moved blocker. It instantiates the authored book, ensures solid collision, replaces the prior active book only after success, and requests navigation rebuilding. A simple fallback book exists if the prefab reference is missing.

  Example:   pointing at terrain behind a solid prop should not let the book pass through that prop. This is why nearest-hit and overlap checks are both needed.

documents.search:
Druid: jumping, slow falling, and the pool cliff

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Characters ,  Overworld .

   What the player does

Space first performs the ordinary jump. Holding Space while airborne slows Druid's fall. Releasing it restores normal falling behavior.

   How it works

 Druid.Update  reads whether Jump is held and calls  CharacterMovement.SetFloating  with the configured glide fall speed (class default 0.35). CharacterMovement owns the vertical-motion implementation. Druid disables root motion so animation does not override the controller position.

On disable, Druid clears the floating flag and disables its actions. This matters when switching characters: the next character must not inherit a stuck glide state.

   The current pool obstacle

 PoolGlideCliff  exposes a landing BoxCollider and tests whether the player is grounded, above its summit, and not swimming.  Chest.RequireDruidLanding  assigns that cliff test. Despite its method name, this path does not check the character is Druid: any character satisfying Supports can interact. This is the current implementation used at pool centers.

The project instructions require a   boat   at the center of each 5×5 pool and a chest on its deck. The cliff is a confirmed mismatch with that requirement, even though it creates a Druid challenge. See the water chapter and gaps checklist.

   What to explain

Gliding is a movement modifier, not free-flight controls. Druid still jumps, falls, and collides with the world. The controller decides when floating can affect vertical speed; the Druid component supplies the held-button intent.

   What the player sees

Approaching an NPC starts dialogue in a speech bubble. Text appears progressively. F completes a typing sentence; a later F advances or performs the final interaction.

   Shared dialogue flow

 NPCBase  finds the active character, measures distance to the collider's closest point, and detects entering/exiting its proximity range. Entering can greet and begin dialogue. A coroutine reveals text at  typingSpeed . Finishing typing shows the interaction prompt. Leaving range or disabling the NPC ends dialogue and stops its coroutine.

Measuring to the collider helps large models: their pivot may be far from the player even when the player stands beside the body. NPCs can rotate toward the player and return to their initial facing.

   Three NPC roles

  Type   What happens after dialogue  
  ---   ---  
  NormalNPC   Presents ordinary dialogue/guide information.  
  InteractableNPC   Opens its ShopInventory, resource selling UI, or assigned UnityEvent.  
  MinigameNPC   Opens a Yes/No challenge prompt for Berdly chemistry or Pink rhythm.  

Accept opens the matching controller. Decline/leave/disable closes the pending prompt. Modal input blocking prevents a number-key answer or F press from also acting in the world.

   Distribution and themes

 NPCSpawner  uses seeded per-chunk placement on valid terrain, avoiding building footprints. DungeonGenerator places guide/friendly NPC content separately. Do not assume every overworld NPC subtype is also spawned in every dungeon.

Minigame NPCs register with  OverworldMusicController . Proximity switches to their exclusive theme, and leaving restores the world music. Berdly battle and rhythm can take ownership of the music state.

Inventory, consumables, HP/SP preview, and Diamond

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Item .

   What the player does

Open Esc → Items, select a consumable, inspect its effect/HP/SP preview, and choose the target character. The UI hides consumable types with zero quantity.

   How quantities work

The Inventory list contains   one InventorySlot per item copy  . Quantity is calculated by counting matching item references/names. It is not stored as a single stack with a quantity field.  OnChanged  tells UI listeners to refresh.

   Using an item

1. InventoryUI verifies that an owned consumable and a valid target are selected.
2. Regular potions cannot target a dead character.
3. An HP-only potion is blocked at full HP; an SP-only potion at full SP; a hybrid at both full.
4.  Consumable.Use(target)  applies configured healing/SP values.
5. Diamond's revive/full-restore flag fills HP and SP.
6. The UI removes one inventory copy, refreshes quantities, and updates the bars.

The current UI supports up to five visible owned consumable types. Effects and descriptions come from the corresponding assets; adding a new asset alone does not automatically add a new configured UI slot.

   Preview versus applying the effect

Preview should show the possible change without spending an item. Only the target action calls Use and removes a copy. Current values are clamped to their maximum by CharacterBase.

   In battle

The same item menu can heal/revive the existing party. After use, InventoryUI refreshes BattleUnit and BattleHUD and emits healing/SP popups. The item data remains shared; the target's live state changes.

documents.search:
Two equipment slots, stat differences, and removing gear

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Equipment .

   What equipment does

Equipment assets hold HP, SP, attack, defense, and crit bonuses plus their shop cost. A character has two equipped slots. Equipment is equipped through its menu, rather than consumed like a potion.

   How the menu works

EquipmentUI presents owned gear, the selected character/slot, the item's description, and differences between current and proposed stats. Confirming delegates the actual stat assignment to  CharacterBase.Equip ; Remove calls  Unequip .

   The stat calculation

For a stat such as attack:   total attack = CharacterData.attack + slot 0 bonus + slot 1 bonus  . The same pattern applies to max HP/SP, defense, and crit. Compare the replaced slot as well as the incoming gear when explaining a preview.

Example: base attack 20, old gear +5, other slot +3 gives 28. Replacing +5 with +8 gives 31, a +3 difference. These are teaching numbers, not the actual asset values.

   Why swapping gear does not heal endlessly

After Equip/Unequip,  ClampStats  reduces current HP/SP only if they exceed the new maximum. Increasing maximum HP does not fill the new space. Removing an HP bonus may reduce current HP to the smaller limit. HUD events then refresh displays.

   Where the gear comes from

Inventory ignores starting Equipment references. Gear can be bought/acquired in gameplay or added with the  equipment  cheat. The cheat catalog references nine configured equipment assets; its number is a catalog fact, not a restriction imposed by the Equipment class.

When explaining “all equipment implemented,” inspect the actual asset catalog and try the UI actions. Having five bonus fields in the class does not alone prove every item is configured.

   What the player sees

   Buying, step by step

documents.title: WFC, weighted entropy, seeded generation, and shoreline rules
headings: Why the shore survives corners and chunk borders
Small piece of the actual code
documents.search:
WFC, weighted entropy, seeded generation, and shoreline rules

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Overworld .

   What WFC does

Wave Function Collapse chooses terrain while respecting allowed neighboring types. A cell begins with a set of possible tiles, called its   domain  . Collapsing chooses one option; propagation removes incompatible options from nearby cells.

   Your game's terrain IDs

  ID   Type   Bit mask  
  ---   ---   ---  
  0   Grass   1  
  1   Water   2  
  2   Sand   4  
  3   Rock   8  

A domain can combine bits.  LandMask  allows grass/sand/rock;  DryMask  allows grass/rock.

   The algorithm in your code

1. Choose the seeded pool pattern for a chunk independently of collapse retries.
2. Begin other cells with LandMask.
3. Reserve the 5×5 water interior, a sand ring, and then a grass/rock ring.
4. Propagate all initial domains through the eight neighbors, including diagonals.
5.  FindLowest  chooses the unresolved cell with lowest weighted Shannon entropy.
6.  PickTerrain  makes a weighted seeded choice among allowed options.
7. Propagate again until every cell is resolved.
8. On contradiction, retry deterministically, up to 16 attempts; exhaustion throws instead of silently replacing water-adjacent cells with grass.
9. Instantiate  tiles tile  , the assigned prefab selected by WFC.

   Why the shore survives corners and chunk borders

Ring distance is  max(dx, dz) , so the sand/dry rings cover corners as squares. Pool origins are inset far enough for both rings to fit within their chunk. Propagation itself stops at chunk bounds; the complete inset pattern is what keeps water away from an unsafe cross-chunk boundary.

   How seeds work

Awake chooses a fresh GUID-derived seed when  randomizeSeedOnPlay  is true. Disabling it uses the explicit seed. Chunk coordinates and salts derive independent random streams, so minimap query/load order does not change content rolls. Continue installs its saved seed.

   Visual blending versus gameplay

Noise supplies terrain preferences and blended painting. It does not replace WFC.  GetTerrainAt  reads the collapsed cell type, while  GetTerrainBlend  returns visual weights. The painter clones/paints TerrainData on instantiated terrain tiles. Resource, swim, and surface queries must use the WFC type.

headings: Small piece of the actual code
documents.search:
Infinite chunks, resources, buildings, NPCs, and decorations

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Overworld .

   What “infinite” means

The player can explore new chunk coordinates while the game keeps nearby chunk objects loaded. It does not instantiate an infinite number of Terrain objects at startup.

   Runtime streaming flow

WFCWorldManager tracks the active character's chunk. On a relevant move or explicit refresh, it generates chunks in view distance and removes distant chunk objects/generated TerrainData. Logical terrain can also be queried/cached without creating the full visible chunk, for example by the minimap.

For a visible chunk, terrain prefabs are created first, then pool/obstacle content and resources. Buildings are placed before NPCs so NPCs can avoid their footprints. Decorations and encounters are added afterward. Physics transforms are synchronized before ground-dependent placement.

   What is randomized

- Grass can contain a tree, mushroom, or rock from one cumulative probability roll per tile.
- Sand can contain cactus from its own probability roll.
- Seeded building/NPC/encounter streams choose locations independently.
- Decorations use biome noise plus a separate seed and a per-chunk count limit.
- Placement reads actual TerrainCollider ground and rejects water or occupied footprints.

 GeneratedResourceMarker  distinguishes decorative objects from collectible gameplay resources. A decoration that looks like a plant should not automatically grant an inventory item.

   Healing spots and landmarks

BuildingSpawner owns healing/dungeon landmark placement. HealingSpot detects proximity, restores HP/SP for all existing party characters, plays feedback, and limits repeat healing with a cooldown (class default three seconds).

   Performance and persistence limits

Chunks reduce the number of live objects, but generation and navigation rebuilding still cost time. There is no fresh performance benchmark in this documentation task. Stable seeds reproduce content positions; explicit progress sets are needed to preserve depletion. Chests/defeated encounters have such sets, while overworld resource removal does not have an equivalent saved list.

Rain and blossom weather are workbook requirements. No weather controller or clearly named weather wiring was located in the reviewed runtime scripts/main scenes; treat those rows as   not located  , pending direct scene inspection.

headings: Small piece of the actual code
documents.search:
5×5 pools, swimming, obstacle chests, and the boat mismatch

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Overworld .

   Water has two parts

The selected WaterTerrain prefab remains the pool bed. The painter changes its runtime TerrainData to create depth, and WaterSurfaceBuilder adds a separate water surface. CharacterMovement uses WFC water plus surface/depth checks to select swimming. Water terrain is excluded from enemy navigation.

   Pool size and shore

Each selected pool is exactly five tiles wide and deep. Its full footprint including the sand ring and grass/rock ring needs a chunk of at least nine tiles. Water can touch water inside the pool. The boundary must follow water → sand → grass/rock even at diagonals.

The midpoint of the pool bounds is the center of tile (3,3), counting from one. With default ten-meter tiles, the water area is 50×50 meters.

   Confirmed unmet boat requirement

Despite its name,  PoolBoatContent.Create  loads  Interaction/PoolGlideCliff , places a rock summit at the midpoint, and puts a chest on it with a grounded summit-landing check.  RequireDruidLanding  is the method name, but that path does not enforce a Druid type check. It does   not   instantiate the assigned boat prefab. WFCWorldManager still has boat prefab/scale/deck-offset fields, but this creation path does not use them.

Your instruction requires a boat at that midpoint and an openable chest on its deck. The cliff implementation fails those boat/deck requirements. The guide records the actual behavior and leaves the game code unchanged.

   Chest progress

PoolBoatContent keeps an opened-chunk HashSet outside the temporary chunk hierarchy. Creating the chunk again restores opened state.  Chest.Opened  records the chunk when the interaction succeeds, and GameSave serializes that list.

The platform obstacle has a separate opened-chest set and an authored platform prefab. Its chest is aligned to the final platform and requires a valid platform landing. Chest seeds use stable world/chunk identity, so loot rolls do not depend on scene instance IDs.

   Surface sound gap

SurfaceAudioSettings defines distinct grass/sand/rock clips and swimming splashes.  WalkingClip(1)  falls back to rock; there is no distinct water walking clip. Swimming audio is present, but the strict requirement for a distinct walking sound for   each of four types   is not fully represented.

headings: Key placement rules in the current code
Small piece of the actual code
documents.search:
Dungeon room graphs, chains, keys, and floor WFC

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Dungeon ,  IUPAC Algorithm .

   Two different generation jobs

DungeonLayout makes the room/door graph and progression data. DungeonGenerator builds rooms and contents from that data. DungeonFloorWFC chooses each room's floor tiles. The floor WFC does not decide the entire dungeon room graph.

   Room graph generation

1. A seeded random walk collects adjacent grid positions.
2. All orthogonally adjacent positions become possible edges with random weights.
3. Kruskal's algorithm sorts edges and uses disjoint sets to reject cycles, producing a minimum spanning tree.
4. The naming algorithm selects the main chain and recursively selects branches.
5. Each room gets a chain index, one-based position, chain degree, random size, and initial kind.
6. The first main-chain room becomes Spawn, the second Guide/Berdly, and the last Boss.
7. Progression keys and door locks are assigned, then the shared chemistry algorithm produces the dungeon name.

The configured default range in DungeonSettings is 14–24 rooms. A selected parent chain is limited to 11 rooms, even when the whole graph has more. Bounded retries reject unsuitable graphs and enforce enough branching for larger dungeons.

   Key placement rules in the current code

Two original keys are placed in distinct non-boss main-chain rooms. Branch endpoints receive original keys to replenish keys spent entering branches. One endpoint at the deepest chain degree is selected to hold the boss key instead. Doors between chains require original keys; doors into the boss room require the boss key.

  Numbering detail:   room Degree here means nesting depth of the selected naming chain. It does not mean the graph-theory count of incident doors.

   Rooms and floor generation

Rooms may be Normal, Treasure, Enemy, Guide, Spawn, or Boss. Dimensions come from settings, independently per room. Floor WFC has brick/slab/cracked/moss options with weights 50/30/14/6. Edges and central crossings allow clear stone types. Moss cannot touch cracked tiles or another moss tile. DungeonGenerator batches floor meshes by material for drawing.

The original workbook's zero on Enemy room is a recorded assessment value; current Generator/EnemySpawner paths exist and should be demonstrated.

Dungeon entry, room doors, keys, treasure, and breakables

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Dungeon .

   Entry requirements

F near an entrance opens the party/entry UI. DungeonSession checks that WiSe and Druid have their ultimates unlocked and the scene is in Build Settings. Complete Berdly/Pink challenges for normal unlocks; the relevant cheats are useful for demonstration in a spare playthrough.

   Travel flow

DungeonSession records the overworld return transform, suspends surface gameplay, loads the dungeon additively, and retains the same party/inventory. A fade hides generation. DungeonIdentity derives a stable entrance identity, so revisiting an entrance can restore its own saved dungeon instead of borrowing another entrance's progress.

Inside the dungeon, DungeonGenerator tracks the current room and nearest eligible interactions. F can open a chest, unlock a door, break a decoration, or use an exit. Door UI distinguishes locked/unlocked states. Room transitions fade the view and place the character in the connected room; the map updates afterward.

   Keys and gate behavior

Original keys are counted and consumed when an original-key door unlocks. A boss gate requires a boss key. The current unlocking code consumes original keys; it tests the boss key without decrementing it. Once a connection is unlocked, its progress is recorded and the player can travel through it.

DungeonGateLift animates the gate. Door highlights/lock icons are feedback; the actual permission comes from connection/key state.

   Room content

- Spawn provides the return/start location.
- Guide/Berdly explains the generated dungeon name.
- Normal rooms have decoration and can include friendly content.
- Treasure rooms provide chests; required key rooms are promoted from Normal to Treasure except the fixed guide.
- Enemy rooms spawn encounters using the shared enemy/battle system.
- Boss room leads to Jevil dialogue and battle.
- Breakable decorations play a timed swing/impact and can drop a coin; configured class defaults include a 10% coin chance.

   Saving during dungeon play

Snapshots retain graph, sizes/kinds, keys, opened chests/doors, broken objects, and remaining coin locations per entrance. Continue restores the first room with progress, not a mid-transition frame.

Exploration camera, zoom, overworld map, and dungeon reveal

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Overworld ,  Dungeon ,  Battle .

   Three related systems

Exploration CameraController follows the selected character and transitions among configured camera views. BattleCamera follows battle units and has its own orbit/first-person behavior. The maps present world information through UI, rather than operating as another gameplay camera.

   Exploration controls

Q/E changes the camera view through the ChangeCam action. The scroll wheel changes field of view within configured limits, with smoothing. CameraController follows CharacterSwitchManager's transform event and can snap immediately after a teleport. Dungeon mode stores/restores camera configuration and provides a steeper view.

The workbook says “rotate camera.” In the exploration implementation, explain the actual configured-view transition rather than claiming an unrestricted free orbit.

   Overworld map

OverworldMinimap creates a Texture2D and paints a player-centered terrain preview from the same world queries. It redraws for a changed tile or seed rather than continuously rebuilding every pixel. Map rotation follows the camera source. M toggles visibility. Hover/scroll map focus allows map zoom without simultaneously zooming the gameplay camera.

Visual colors can use terrain blend information, but the collapsed WFC terrain remains the gameplay type. Minimap prequeries can fill logical terrain caches without instantiating all visible objects; chunk generation uses independent seeds to avoid query-order changes.

   Dungeon map

Rooms and door connections form the grid. Visiting a room marks it visited and reveals it plus its immediate neighbors. Revealed and visited are separate sets. The active character portrait marks the current room. Camera rotation rotates the map; UI panning moves the preview without rebuilding the texture.

 showmain  reveals/highlights the main chain;  revealall  reveals all rooms and colors by chain degree. These reveal commands do not mean those rooms were actually visited.

   Battle camera

BattleCamera follows the selected party member, or focuses an enemy during its action. Q/E orbits, scroll changes distance/tilt, and RandaL's ultimate temporarily enters first person. Camera state is restored after special sequences.

headings: Small piece of the actual code
documents.search:
Enemy FSM, navigation, Skeleton/Minion attacks, and variants

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Enemies .

   What an FSM is

A finite state machine chooses one named state and performs that state's behavior. Your encounter enemy has Idle, Patrol, Chase, Attack, and OutOfSight. Transitions reset relevant timers and pending attack impact.

  State   Behavior and exit  
  ---   ---  
  Idle   Waits stationary; after three seconds, tries a patrol destination.  
  Patrol   Moves toward a seeded random reachable point near home; returns to Idle on arrival/timeout.  
  Chase   Repaths toward the detected player.  
  Attack   Stops, faces the player, winds up, and checks/launches an impact.  
  OutOfSight   Stops and visibly searches left/right; returns to Idle after about 1.5 seconds.  

   Navigation and detection

NavMeshAgent follows valid paths rather than walking in a straight line through obstacles. Patrol samples a random point within home radius and requires a complete path. Chase is not restricted to that patrol radius. Detection considers height/range, with extra tracking tolerance. A line-of-sight ray rejects blocked attacks. Water terrain is excluded from generated exploration navigation.

   What starts combat

Skeleton's actual melee impact must overlap the active character. Minion launches EncounterProjectile; actual projectile collision starts the battle. Moving out of range or behind a blocker can cancel/intercept the hit. Merely seeing the enemy is not itself the battle trigger.

   Battle variants

Veterans are larger/purple with enemy red highlighting. Skeleton veteran attacks three times with post-defense scales 1, 0.5, and 0.25. Minion veteran fires two projectiles. Damage has a minimum of one, so tiny later hits still deal one.

BattleEnemyMotion handles procedural sword/body/recoil feedback around the imported models. Settings provide attack/laser sounds. Stable encounter identities let BattleSession remember defeated enemies across chunk reloads and saves.

For FSM explanation, name both the   condition   that changes state and the   action   performed in the state. Listing five labels alone does not explain the machine.

headings: Small piece of the actual code
documents.search:
Encounters, party turns, AP, cover, victory, and returns

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Battle .

   Entering a battle

BattleSession remembers encounter identity and return position, suspends exploration, and loads BattleScene. BattleController randomly selects one of three saved layouts and builds its NavMesh. It reuses the party's CharacterBase instances and spawns a group including the encountered species. Battle layout randomness includes runtime time, so a fixed overworld seed alone does not guarantee the same battle layout.

   The turn model

Player, Enemy, Acting, Victory, and GameOver are separate phases. You can switch living characters during the party turn. Each has a movement origin/radius and   two AP  . Skill/ultimate slots spend one AP; basic attack spends no AP but locks movement. SP, cooldown, phase, living state, and unlock gates also control usability.

Press T to end the party turn. Each living enemy resets movement, chooses the closest living target, moves within its range, and attacks. Party turns reset AP/movement and advance character cooldowns. Cooldowns are stored on CharacterBase and persist between battles.

   Damage, healing, and cover

 BattleUnit.Damage :   max(1, round((raw attack − defense) × scale))  . A shield consumes one stack and blocks the complete hit before that calculation. Dead targets are excluded.

Cover intercepts projectiles and has HP/state feedback; at half health it becomes shorter. Projectile travel/collision determines the struck object, so selecting a target does not guarantee a shot bypasses cover. HP/SP changes create popups and refresh HUDs. Enemy-turn presentation makes unrelated units/cover translucent to emphasize the action.

   Death and results

A dead party unit has a stone appearance, disabled hitbox, and cannot act. Diamond through the existing item menu can revive it. All party dead means GameOver. All enemies defeated means Victory; total enemy EXP is granted to every party member and level changes are displayed.

Victory returns to the recorded encounter location and records its stable defeated ID. Save & Quit stores progress and return context, not an exact paused projectile. Dungeon battle saves resume through the dungeon's first-room restoration.

   UI and speed

BattleHUD displays portraits, HP/SP, skill icons/cooldowns, AP, turn messages, and results. Hover shows skill data; selection shows affected area. Key 5 toggles sequence speed between 1× and 4×. Special dodge/rhythm timing follows its own rules rather than simply accelerating every input window.

headings: Small piece of the actual code
documents.search:
WiSe battle skills: crescent, shields, dragon, and dodge

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Skills .

   Where the abilities live

WiSe.cs owns exploration cutting. WiSe's battle abilities are the  characterIndex == 0  branches inside BattleController. BattleSkill assets supply name, description, icon, SP, cooldown, range, and radius; the controller supplies the actual effect.

  Slot/key   Behavior  
  ---   ---  
  Basic / 1   A facing semicircle hits live enemies/cover with raw  25 + Attack . A/D rotates the preview. A kill resets movement and basic cooldown, and heals ceil(5% max HP).  
  First skill / 2   Adds one shield to living allies within radius, capped at three. Each stack cancels one complete incoming hit.  
  Second skill / 3   Dragonfire selects enemies inside the aimed radius and launches five fireballs per target in round-robin order.  
  Ultimate / 4   Flurry Rush enables a two-turn dodge stance after its unlock gate.  

   Dragonfire details

Raw total per target is the controller's magic-adjusted rounded  (60 + Attack × 1.1) × 0.7 . Integer division/remainder spreads that raw total over five projectiles. Defense is applied on each projectile hit, and cover can intercept them. Therefore “five shots” does not necessarily equal five successful enemy hits or total raw damage after defense.

Round robin means target A, B, C for volley 1, then A, B, C for volley 2, continuing up to five. Launches do not wait for each impact. The sequence waits until pending projectiles finish before returning to player phase.

   Dodge timing

Space is sampled during an incoming eligible attack. Perfect is 0.60–0.85 seconds, successful dodge input extends through 0.95 seconds, and missed/late-outside-window input fails. A perfect dodge permits up to five right-click counters within three seconds. The normal enemy sequence fast-forward does not shorten this dodge input window.

WiSe's ultimate is unlocked by winning Berdly's chemistry challenge, or explicitly by the  luluspresent  cheat. SP/AP/cooldown can still prevent casting after unlock.

  Slot/key   Behavior  
  ---   ---  
  Basic / 1   Locks a live enemy in range. A/D cycles candidates. Fires a projectile with magic-adjusted  10 + Attack .  
  First skill / 2   Restores SP to living allies in radius and adds a two-turn magic buff.  
  Second skill / 3   Opens portal state and reduces the other three cooldown slots by one, never below zero.  
  Ultimate / 4   Arcane Barrage enters first person for up to ten seconds. Hold/release left mouse to charge/fire.  

   Buff and portal rules

Ordinary first skill restores rounded  (5 + Attack) × 1.6  SP and grants a 30% magic buff. Portal-empowered use multiplies that restoration by 1.5 and grants 40%. The helper  Magic  applies the actor's current magicBuff multiplier to raw magic damage.

Portal empowers the next non-portal ability and is then consumed. Empowered basic projectiles can bounce through up to two additional nearby living enemies. Portal reduces RandaL's own other cooldowns; it does not loop over every party member's cooldowns. Explain this concrete scope when demonstrating the rubric's “Lower all cooldown by 1.”

   Arcane Barrage

The camera becomes first person, a crosshair appears, and party visuals become partly transparent. Charge caps at 1.5 seconds. Releasing launches toward the center-camera ray, with size/damage interpolated by charge and a shot interval of 0.5 seconds. A near-full portal-empowered charge enables bounce behavior.

At completion the controller waits for outstanding shots, stops charge sound, hides the crosshair, restores third-person camera, and restores ally visibility. Opening the menu pauses the sequence/charge audio until resumed.

RandaL's ultimate has no HasUltimate requirement in  CanUse ; the unlock check explicitly exempts selected character index 1. AP/SP/cooldown still apply.

Druid.cs supplies exploration floating. BattleController's  characterIndex == 2  branch supplies combat effects.

  Slot/key   Behavior

  Basic / 1   Radiant Chorus bursts at the aimed point, damages enemies, and heals living allies within radius.  
  First skill / 2   Enrapturing Melody pulls initially selected enemies toward Druid over five sequence seconds.

The controller captures targets inside the initial radius, then repeatedly calls PullTowards. Forced movement also shifts their movement origin so the later range clamp does not snap them back. The five-second effect follows sequence speed, so fast-forward can shorten its real duration.

Grand Ensemble hides Druid's original renderers, spawns the performance model, reframes the camera, faces enemies toward it, and stops the introductory sound before the rhythm countdown. Jevil dialogue, summoning, kidnapping, and five dodge patterns

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Boss Battle .

   Before the fight

Approaching the boss opens BattleBossDialogue. F completes/advances its text. The battle session then enters the boss version of BattleScene with its music, group, and Jevil unit.

   Jevil's turn

The controller chooses the nearest living party target, summons ordinary enemies, relocates Jevil on valid ground, and attempts to place the target near him. It then chooses one of five heart-dodging patterns in BattleBossGame.

   Five patterns (human numbering)

  Pattern   Implementation  
  ---   ---  
  1   Jevil fires a five-spade fan toward the heart from outside the arena.  
  2   A heart bomb tracks briefly, then splits into four moving rotating hearts.  
  3   Four scythes remain as one formation with individual inner motion, outer orbit, and blade spin.  
  4   Ten spades around the boundary launch toward center in alternating sequence order.  
  5   Rapid spades rise from randomized bottom positions.  

Code uses pattern indices 0–4. Each pattern runs for up to ten seconds or until the target dies. WASD moves the heart within the UI box. Projectile motion has a 1.5× multiplier independent of heart speed.

   Collision and damage

Most projectiles compare distance with the heart. Scythes use blade/handle segment checks so transparent sprite corners are safe. A hit calls  victim.Damage(boss.Attack, 1 + enemies/100f) . BattleUnit subtracts defense before scaling and applies the one-damage minimum; a shield may block the hit.

After a hit the heart has 1.5 seconds of invincibility and flashes. The panel hides and all bullets return to their pools when the sequence ends. Pools reuse UI Images rather than instantiating/destroying every wave repeatedly.

The saved MovementBox has square sizing in the existing presentation notes; verify it visually at the target screen resolution. An old Cheats.md statement that Jevil is unimplemented is stale relative to these current scripts.

documents.search:
Berdly chemistry battle: answers, timer, attack, and defend

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Minigame .

   What the player does

Accept Berdly's challenge, choose Attack or Defend, and answer molecule-name questions using the four answer buttons or 1–4. The minigame has its own player/Berdly HP and screen states; it is separate from BattleController's 3D party battle.

   One turn

1. Choose the action and start a timed question sequence.
2. BerdlyChemistry supplies a molecule, correct name, and four shuffled answers.
3. The molecule view renders the graph and the UI displays the choices.
4. A correct answer increases correctAnswers and adjusts the remaining timer by  7 − 0.5 × correctAnswers , clamped to 0–20 seconds.
5. A wrong answer or expired timer ends guessing.
6. The chosen action resolves, then Berdly attacks if still alive.
7. The next move selection opens unless victory/defeat was reached.

   Attack and defend

Attack damage is configured damagePerAnswer × correctAnswers (class default 10). The sonic-wave effect applies damage at impact, so HP change matches the attack animation cue.

Defend heals configured healPerAnswer × correctAnswers, limited by the minigame's 100 HP (class default six per answer). Choosing defend grants protection for two enemy attacks. Protected damage is reduced by 50%, and each protected attack consumes one protection turn. Berdly damage is configurable (class default 33).

   Win and unlock

On victory, FinishBattle unlocks WiSe's ultimate on the existing WiSe instance(s) and displays a result modal. Defeat allows retry. This unlock can later satisfy one dungeon-entry requirement.

   Practice and rendering limits

Questions target 2–11 carbons with simple branches. The naming code also supports recursive dungeon branches, so don't assume the two generators use identical complexity limits. The graph holds bonds and drawing coordinates separately. The view draws the graph; it does not decide the answer.

The timer/turn resolution continues while the cheat console captures gameplay keys. Use a spare playthrough when demonstrating  tpagacor  because it grants the normal victory unlock.

documents.search:
The shared molecule and dungeon naming algorithm

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    IUPAC Algorithm ,  Dungeon ,  Minigame .

   What is shared

 BerdlyMolecule  stores nodes (carbons/rooms), undirected bonds (connections/doors), and drawing coordinates.  BerdlyChemistry  generates questions and names graphs. DungeonLayout reuses SelectChain/Name to divide a dungeon into chains and name it.

The code follows the project's alkane/alkyl notation, including its hyphen before the parent alkane. This chapter explains that implementation, not a claim to cover every chemical IUPAC rule or molecule type.

   Building a question graph

A random walk collects unique grid points. Adjacent grid points get random-weight edges. Kruskal sorts them and joins only different disjoint sets, creating a connected acyclic carbon tree. Question generation rejects unsuitable/simple-branch limits with bounded retries and has a known fallback tree.

   Naming, step by step

1.  BestPath  considers possible endpoints within the selected component.
2. Prefer the longest chain, then branch/locant tie-breaks.
3. For the top-level chain consider orientation so branch locants favor the earlier/lower arrangement.
4. For each off-chain connected component, recursively call NamePart from its attachment root.
5. Group identical branch names, collect their one-based positions, and apply multiplier prefixes.
6. Sort branch-name groups and append the parent alkane from the naming table.
7. A nested branch name is wrapped in parentheses using the project's recursive notation.

The maximum selected chain is 11.  LongestChainLength  uses tree-distance searches to detect the diameter length, but the actual tie-breaking chain selection comes from BestPath. Do not confuse the longest-length helper with the full numbering algorithm.

   A small worked example

Imagine a five-carbon parent path with a one-carbon side branch at the second carbon. The table supplies  pentane  and  methyl ; numbering gives locant 2; the project's naming output is  2-methyl-pentane . Reversing that drawing must still prefer locant 2 over 4. Drawing coordinates do not define the name: bonds do.

   Wrong answers

MakeQuestion creates nearby graph mutations by adding one carbon, names them, removes duplicates/correct matches, and shuffles three distractors plus the correct answer. Very small molecules supplement distractors with nearby alkanes. Distractors are generated data, not four hardcoded button labels.

Dungeon “degree 1” is the parent naming chain; degree 2/3 means recursively nested branch chains, not carbon bond degree.

   Scripts to read

- BerdlyMolecule.cs — included copy.
- DungeonLayout.cs — included copy.
- BerdlyMoleculeView.cs — included copy.

   Small piece of the actual code

From BerdlyMolecule.cs (line 205). This is an excerpt; continue in the full script for context.

   csharp
string NamePart(BerdlyMolecule molecule, HashSet<int  included, int root)
{
    var chain = BestPath(molecule, included, root);
    if (chain.Count   MaximumChain)
        throw new ArgumentException("The longest carbon chain cannot exceed " + MaximumChain + ".");
    var groups = new SortedDictionary<string, List<int  (StringComparer.Ordinal);
    var onChain = new HashSet<int (chain);
    for (int i = 0; i < chain.Count; i++)
        foreach (int neighbour in molecule.Bonds chain i  )
        {
            if (!included.Contains(neighbour)    onChain.Contains(neighbour)) continue;
            var branch = Component(molecule, neighbour, included, onChain);
            string name = NamePart(molecule, branch, neighbour);
            if (!groups.TryGetValue(name, out var positions)) groups name  = positions = new List<int ();
            positions.Add(i + 1);
        }
    if (groups.Count == 0) return root < 0 ? alkanes chain.Count - 1  : alkyls chain.Count - 1 ;
   

   Demonstrate it yourself

Trace a hand-built simple branched graph through BestPath, Component, NamePart, and the name tables. Explain chain length, direction, branch grouping, and final formatting. Compare the dungeon name with its room/door graph.

   Explain it in one answer

“The bonds define a tree. We select and number a parent chain, recursively name off-chain components, group repeated branches, then format the name from the supplied tables.”

headings: Small piece of the actual code
documents.search:
Pink rhythm: beatmap parsing, tap/hold judgements, and score

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Rythm Game ,  Minigame ,  Skills .

   What the player does

Accept Pink's challenge and use W/A/S/D as notes reach the target. Tap notes need a press; hold notes need a press followed by sustained input. The UI shows score, judgement, stamina, moving notes, and the Mario/Pink stage model.

   Beatmap format

PinkBeatmap.Parse requires a  start=  audio offset and a  notes=  count.  1 t=1000  is a W tap at one second.  2 t_start=2000 t_end=3500  is an A hold from two to 3.5 seconds. Note timestamps are milliseconds; the parsed model stores seconds. Keys 1/2/3/4 map to W/A/S/D. Invalid headers, mismatched counts, or a hold ending before its start throw format errors.

   Clock and rendering

PinkRhythmController schedules music/countdown and uses the audio DSP clock to advance play. It supplies pressed/held key masks to the rules. UI note positions are drawn from note time versus current time, and a visual pool reuses note objects.  timingOffset  is the configurable alignment adjustment.

   Tap judgement and rewards

  Judgement   Absolute timing error at most   Score weight   Stamina change  
  ---   ---   ---   ---  
  Perfect   95 ms   1.00   +3.5  
  Great   161 ms   0.85   +2.5  
  Good   249 ms   0.65   +1.5  
  Ok   336 ms   0.45   +0.7  
  Bad   468 ms   0.20   −2  
  Miss   Beyond 468 ms/unplayed   0   −3.5  

Each note is worth  100000 / total notes × judgement weight . DisplayScore rounds and caps at 100,000. Stamina stays in 0–100; zero fails. Extra unmatched key presses do not receive an invented stamina penalty.

   Hold judgement

The first press gets its timing judgement. Held duration is accumulated until release/end. At least 80% completion preserves the first judgement; 45–under 80% becomes Ok; under 45% becomes Bad. An initial Bad/Miss is not upgraded by holding. A hold is finalized/scored once, rather than scored every frame.

   Unlock and battle reuse

Completing without failure at   84,000 or more   unlocks Druid's ultimate. Grand Ensemble uses the same controller/rules with a shorter battle chart and a callback returning accuracy. It pauses/restores the surrounding music and restores its chart settings afterward.

The workbook spells its supporting sheet  Rythm Game ; the guide uses correct “rhythm” spelling while preserving that source locator.

documents.search:
Cheat console, area checks, and all supported commands

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Cheats .

   Opening and submitting

Press Ctrl in gameplay to open the console. Type/paste a complete known code; it runs automatically when it matches. Esc or Ctrl closes it. Matching ignores case and surrounding spaces. A successful command clears the input so another command can be entered.

The console captures gameplay keys without pausing the running world/music. A timing challenge may continue while you type. It rejects wrong-area commands and dungeon travel. Pink rhythm must be closed before these commands execute.

  Area   Code   Actual effect  
  ---   ---   ---  
  Overworld   Nerdlumarco / Nerdluryuu   Teleport to nearby loaded Berdly.  
  Overworld   wibulupaul   Teleport to nearby loaded Pink.  
  Overworld   cashgrab   Add 1,000 gold.  
  Overworld   equipment   Add one of every item in the equipment catalog.  
  Overworld   drain   Set party HP to one.  
  Overworld   luluspresent   Unlock WiSe ultimate on the live party.  
  Overworld   lastday   Unlock Druid ultimate on the live party.  
  Overworld   724   Find a dungeon entrance; if absent, try the existing seeded prefab-spawn path.  
  Overworld   spawnpoint   Return to the overworld origin, streaming ground if necessary.

  Dungeon   skipskip   Move before boss and provide a Boss Key.  
  Battle   tpagacor   Defeat the current 3D battle group or win Berdly, using the normal victory path.  
  Battle   evalcore   Set party HP to one; also drains the Berdly minigame player where applicable.  

   Why teleports still use the world rules

Targets must be available in loaded content except the explicit dungeon/origin fallback. Landing selection checks clear dry Terrain using the WFC type, not just the visible blended color.  724  does not hand-build a replacement world: it asks the existing building spawner for the assigned dungeon prefab and remembers the forced landmark.

   Teaching and persistence

Unlock/gold/inventory cheats change live state and can be saved. They do not rewrite shared CharacterData assets. Use a spare playthrough if you want to preserve normal progression. Current CheatCodes supports the 3D battle too; the older Cheats.md sentence limiting battle cheats to Berdly is stale.

{

documents.search:
Audio routing, footsteps, particles, highlights, and UI feedback

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    General ,  Characters ,  NPC ,  Overworld ,  Main Menu ,  Skills .

   Shared audio routing

GameAudio routes music/SFX through separate mixer groups. Title, footsteps, NPC greeting, dungeon, and battle sources use that route. OverworldMusicController tracks NPC proximity and special owners so Berdly themes, chemistry battle, and rhythm do not overlap the world track unintentionally.

   Distance-based surface sound

CharacterSurfaceAudio measures horizontal movement since the last frame. It accumulates distance and plays after the configured step spacing. Idle, airborne movement, large teleports, menus, and breaking actions reset/suppress steps. Swimming has separate splash spacing and clips; entering water can immediately play a splash.

For grounded walking it asks  WFCWorldManager.GetTerrainAt . SurfaceAudioSettings maps grass and sand explicitly and everything else to rock. The saved asset has three distinct dry-terrain clip references and three swimming clips. The missing distinct water walking clip is documented as a requirement gap.

   What makes the feedback visible

- Character switching can instantiate a switch particle prefab.
- ObjectHighlight and renderer/outline configuration distinguish player/NPC/enemy objects.
- Battle popups display damage/healing, and status visuals display shields/buffs.
- Dungeon arrival titles, coin sounds, room fades, gate lifts, and swing/impact cues communicate changes.
- GameplayHudVisibility coordinates exploration HUD visibility around overlays and battle transitions.

   Responsive UI and post processing

Scenes contain Unity UI and global Volume objects; BattleScene has its own post-processing object. Anchors, CanvasScaler configuration, text sizing, and actual resolution determine layout. Merely using RectTransform does not establish that every screen is responsive. Inspect each major overlay at different supported aspect ratios.

Visual feedback is separate from gameplay permission: a shield icon must agree with BattleUnit.shields, a door highlight must agree with lock/key state, and a blended shore must agree with WFC terrain. Asset/scene assignments determine whether the authored clips/materials actually appear in a player build.
