   What this review establishes

These guides were written from the supplied workbook, the current local source, core scenes/assets, and older Docs as secondary context. No Unity build, Play-mode session, or editor fixture was run for this documentation task. Existing PASS files are historical evidence only.

   Confirmed mismatches with your project instructions

  Requirement   Current source evidence   Result  
  ---   ---   ---  
  Boat at every 5×5 pool center, chest on its deck   PoolBoatContent creates PoolGlideCliff and places a landing-gated chest on its summit. The boat field is unused in this creation path.   Unmet boat/deck requirement.  
  Distinct walking sound for all four terrain types   SurfaceAudioSettings has grass/sand/rock and swimming; WalkingClip(1) returns rock.   Unmet distinct water walking-sound mapping.  

The code does implement prefab-based seeded WFC, Terrain tiles, inset 5×5 water with diagonal sand/dry rings, separate swimming surface, explicit fixed/fresh seeds, and WFC gameplay queries. Source implementation is not a new runtime certification.

   Workbook features not fully established

- Rain/blossom weather: no controller or clearly named main-scene wiring located in this review. Inspect ParticleSystem/Animator assets and run the intended behavior before claiming completion.
- Title character models, different animations, and Play animation: require direct title visual/animation review.
- Creativity/design, responsive UI, and optimization: human judgement/runtime inspection needed. Streaming/pooling/batching are mechanisms, not a benchmark or official score.
- Dungeon shop distribution: dungeon guide/friendly placement is present, but don't infer every interactable/shop subtype exists there from NPC inheritance alone.
- Four terrain audio assignments, boat/deck placement, and all corner/chunk shoreline cases: use the dedicated requirements as the expected result when playtesting, not the current behavior as the expected result.

   Important limits

Overworld removed resources do not have a saved depletion list. Dungeon saves resume in their first room. Mid-battle saves restore encounter context, not the exact action frame. Portal cooldown reduction loops over RandaL's own other slots. Naming follows the project's recursive tree notation.

   Existing editor tools

The script reference has every Editor helper and its actual MenuItem where present. Checks exercise behavior; Setup/Builder tools mutate scene/assets and are not equivalent to harmless read-only checks. Run a relevant check deliberately in Unity and read its output; do not call an old result a fresh pass.

In-game menu, Resources, Stats, previews, and Save & Quit

Guide home · Controls · Script index

  Workbook areas:    Battle ,  Overworld ,  Dungeon .

   What the player opens

Esc opens the gameplay menu. MenuTabManager selects the default tab and switches between configured panels. Items, equipment, resources, stats, audio settings, and quit each have a separate UI owner.

   Panel responsibilities

- InventoryUI selects consumables and their character targets, validates use, and refreshes quantities/HP/SP.
- EquipmentUI selects gear/slots and shows stat differences.
- ResourceMenuPanelUI reads resource counts from Inventory; it does not generate world resources.
- StatsMenuPanelUI reads CharacterBase's current/base-plus-equipment stats.
- GameAudioMenuUI changes shared audio settings.
- QuitMenuUI offers Keep Playing or Save & Quit and displays save failures.
- MenuStatBar applies current values and preview presentation to the configured UI bars.

   Input and battle behavior

MenuToggle subscribes to the Player Menu action. In a 3D battle it delegates to BattleSession.OpenMenu instead of using the ordinary exploration toggle. Battle controllers check MenuOpen to suspend action timing and refresh party state when returning.

Outside battle, NPCChallengePrompt.BlocksGameplayInput combines active menus/modal systems to stop world movement/interactions. Do not assume every overlay pauses global time: the cheat console explicitly allows time/music to continue, while individual systems have their own blocking/pause rules.

   Preview is not a purchase/use

Hovering/selecting an item or gear shows a possible stat change. Confirming a consumable removes one copy; equipping modifies a slot. Reading a preview must not alter actual HP/SP or spend gold. The character's methods remain authoritative for applied state.

   Saving and quitting

QuitMenuUI calls the save operation, waits for success, then returns to TitleScene. Failure leaves the player in the current game with a message. Saving during dungeon/scene travel is rejected until travel finishes.

   Scripts to read

From MenuToggle.cs (line 43). This is an excerpt; continue in the full script for context.

   csharp
public void ToggleMenu()
{
    if (BattleSession.IsActive) { BattleSession.Instance.OpenMenu(); return; }
    if (NPCChallengePrompt.BlocksGameplayInput) return;
    if (menuUI != null)
    {
        bool opening = !menuUI.activeSelf;
        if (opening && menuTabs != null)
            menuTabs.ShowDefaultTab();

        menuUI.SetActive(opening);
    }
}

Open Esc, switch every configured tab, and inspect current values versus previews. Close the menu and confirm controls resume. In battle, use an item through the same menu and observe updated HUD state. Save & Quit through a spare slot.
